label: churn200-s2
summary: The model predicts customer churn as the sigmoid of a direct linear score plus eight nonlinear parts, added on the logit; the annotated model reproduces the network on every training row (largest absolute error 1.3e-15). Two parts carry the ranking. The direct terms raise risk for heavy day-time users, international-plan holders and customers without a voice-mail plan; replacing them by their mean lowers the training AUC from 0.9077 to 0.4443. A service-call gate makes day minutes act in a V-shape: for low and moderate day use it adds risk that grows with each customer-service call, and it closes once day minutes pass a threshold that rises with the number of calls (switching it off lowers the AUC to 0.7348). For a typical customer with one call, predicted risk falls from 9% at very low day use to 2% at moderate use and rises to 77% at heavy use; the 318 training customers with four or more calls have observed churn 50.0%. The remaining parts are small: an evening-usage hinge that damps the evening-minutes effect (from lower use in Arkansas), a second service-call hinge shut in West Virginia, a night-charge hinge, and offsets for single states (North Carolina, Arizona, Tennessee, South Carolina, Idaho, Wyoming), each resting on a small number of training customers, and an offset for one area code.
